response.strategyText: She adjusted her gloves and took a deep breath before stepping onto the field.

We approach this encounter with a disciplined, conservative posture. Our Weedle and Caterpie are young and fragile; they must avoid unnecessary risk. Our primary concerns are preserving both companions, controlling the pace of the engagement, and preventing the opponent from establishing momentum. We will prioritize status-oriented moves—String Shot to slow faster foes, Effect Nightmare and Effect Def Plus 2 to impose pressure and reduce incoming damage. We will conserve our limited move-change budget and avoid committing to offensive actions unless the opponent reveals a pattern we can safely exploit. Because the opposing party and lead are entirely unknown, we treat all predictions as hypotheses and will adjust our sequence only after observing the first exchange. Our style will be patient and adaptive: wait for the opponent to act, respond with the least risky effective option, and retreat to preserve partner health if the situation deteriorates. We enter with no healing items, so every turn must be calculated to keep both Weedle and Caterpie operational through the battle.
